name: Zauq
bio: Zauq is called in the book a celebrated poet at the court of Bahadur Shah (r. 1837–57) and his teacher in the arts of verse, compiler of an anthology of poems, said to have written one hundred thousand verses and still highly popular and much quoted.

The one piece given here is drawn from Hindustani Lyrics (London: The Sufi Publishing Society, 1919), in the English verse of Inayat Khan and Jessie Duncan Westbrook. It is a free rendering, not a literal translation, and the original Urdu poem is untitled; it is named here by its first line.

poems.title: O Tyrannous One, when from my heart was drawn
poems.author: Zauq
poems.translator: trans. Inayat Khan and Jessie Duncan Westbrook (1919)
poems.text:
O Tyrannous One, when from my heart was drawn
    The fatal arrow, like a scarlet flood
My life gushed forth; but yet the one word Hope
    Was written in my blood.

Why should the Cosmos turn its wheel of worlds
    If not to search for thee eternally?
Why should the tireless Sun arise each morn
    If not to look for thee?

Alas my fate! before you came to me
    Already had I felt the touch of Death,
Nor was I spared before thy worshipped feet
    To offer up my breath.

For long, throughout the world, I sought for thee,
    Through weary years and ages of unrest;
At last I found thee hidden in my arms
    Within my breast!
